critical.issue: No content validation: uploading a 14-byte non-PDF ('not-a-real-pdf', content-type application/pdf) produced job status 'done' and created a full bogus project ('Unknown Property', ref RTF-2026-0161..0163) instead of erroring. After the OCR fallback, if extracted text is empty/too short the job should end as 'error' with a user-facing message and must not persist a project.

minor.issue: Returns 200 {'status':'analyzing'} for a non-existent template id (no existence check before create_task); should be 404. Reproduced by tests/test_templates.py::test_analyze_unknown_template.

Path allow-list uses str.startswith, so junk scalar paths that merely share a prefix are accepted, e.g. path='partnerZZZ' or 'statusfoo' write new top-level fields to the project doc. Use an exact-match set for scalar fields and prefix matching only for the dotted ones ('property.', 'measures.', ...).

_partner_for() fabricates a partner from a hash of the ref whenever 'partner' is falsy, so (a) a user cannot ever clear/unassign a partner (saving '' shows 'Unassigned' optimistically, then a partner reappears on reload) and (b) invented partner names are indistinguishable from real data. Consider returning null and rendering 'Unassigned', or only defaulting at seed time.
find(...).to_list(100) while 57 templates already exist — silently truncates once the library passes 100. Paginate or raise the limit.

seed_admins never re-hashes an existing admin's password ('never overwrite a changed password'), so if the SEED_ADMINS password is rotated the documented credential stops working and a restart cannot restore it. Playbook expects the seed to update the hash when the seed password changes.

CORS_ORIGINS='*' with allow_credentials=True. Starlette echoes the request Origin so browsers currently work (verified: preflight does not return '*' with credentials), but explicit origins are the documented requirement.

ui_bugs.issue: Delete button is opacity:0 until the row is hovered (measured 0 -> 1 on hover), so it is undiscoverable on touch devices and invisible to keyboard-only focus.
React console warning: 'Missing Description or aria-describedby={undefined} for DialogContent' each time the palette opens — add a DialogDescription / aria-describedby.

integration_issues.issue: Saving an empty partner optimistically shows 'Unassigned' but after reload the backend hash fallback repopulates a partner name — the UI state and persisted state disagree.

action_items: Validate extracted document content in run_import_job (post-OCR) and fail the job instead of creating an 'Unknown Property' project from an unreadable upload.
Return 404 from POST /api/templates/{tid}/analyze for unknown ids.
Tighten ALLOWED_PATCH_PREFIXES to exact matches for scalar fields (prefix match currently allows 'partnerZZZ', 'statusfoo', ...).
Decide the partner fallback semantics so a partner can actually be cleared (return null + render 'Unassigned').
Make the build-up row delete button visible on focus (focus-visible:opacity-100) as well as hover.
Optional: raise/paginate the GET /api/templates 100-doc limit; add DialogDescription to the command palette.
critical_code_review_comments: run_import_job has no guard on extracted text length, so the LLM invents an entire project from noise — the job should short-circuit to status 'error' when the combined extracted text (after _ocr_pdf) is below a sane threshold.

update_project_field writes payload.value straight into $set with no per-path type validation; e.g. 'measures.0.buildup' will accept a string or an object and break the workspace/pack renderers. Validate array/number shapes for the known paths.
DesignWorkspace.jsx is 777 lines and mixes navigation, 8 section renderers, EditableCell and MeasureDetail — split MeasureDetail/EditableCell into their own modules (guideline: <700 lines).
addLayer/removeLayer rewrite the whole buildup array with no optimistic-concurrency check; two tabs editing the same measure will silently clobber each other.

rca_of_the_issue: Phantom-project bug: import_project stores the upload and queues run_import_job, which calls extract_pdf_text (+_ocr_pdf fallback) and passes whatever it gets to the LLM. With an unparseable file both extractors return ~nothing, but there is no minimum-content check, so the LLM is asked to draft a project from an empty prompt and returns a plausible skeleton which is persisted as a real project and the job is marked 'done'. Reproduce: POST /api/projects/import with files=('x.pdf', b'not-a-real-pdf'), types='assessment', then GET /api/projects — a new 'Unknown Property' ref appears.
